Silicon photonics went from a specialist VC niche to one of the hottest consolidation stories in semiconductors between 2023 and mid-2026, driven almost entirely by the AI datacenter interconnect bottleneck. Optim VC estimates more than $15B changed hands in the sector between late 2025 and mid-2026 alone. The watershed events: Marvell's acquisition of Celestial AI (announced Dec 2, 2025) for $3.25B upfront ($1B cash + 27.2M shares) with earn-outs taking it to ~$5.5B, closed Q1 2026; Nvidia's ~$6.5B photonics supply-chain push in early 2026 ($2B each into Coherent and Lumentum as growth equity plus multibillion purchase commitments, and up to $3.2B into Corning); and Nokia's completed $2.3B (€2.19B) acquisition of Infinera on Feb 28, 2025. A dense second tier of exits followed: Ciena bought Nubis Communications for $270M cash (Sept 2025), Credo bought DustPhotonics for ~$1.3B ($750M cash + $123M stock, up to $430M more in earn-outs, closed May 28, 2026), Molex bought Teramount for $430M (closed May 7, 2026, only ~10 months after Teramount's $50M round), AMD quietly acquired Enosemi (May 2025), and GlobalFoundries acquired both Advanced Micro Foundry and InfiniLink (Nov 2025) to become the largest dedicated silicon photonics foundry.

On the venture side, mega-rounds concentrated in co-packaged optics / optical I/O for AI scale-up. Ayar Labs closed a $500M Series E on March 3, 2026 at a $3.75B valuation (led by Neuberger Berman; ARK, Insight, QIA, Sequoia Global Equities, 1789 Capital, plus strategics AMD, MediaTek, Alchip, Nvidia; $870M total raised). Lightmatter raised a $400M Series D in Oct 2024 at $4.4B led by T. Rowe Price (~$850M total). PsiQuantum, the photonic quantum outlier, raised $1B in Sept 2025 at $7B valuation (BlackRock, Temasek, Baillie Gifford, with NVentures). Below the mega-rounds, a healthy Series A/B market formed: Xscape Photonics ($44M Series A Sept 2024 with Cisco Investments and Nvidia, plus $37M extension led by Addition in March 2026, ~$81M Series A total), Avicena ($65M Series B led by Tiger Global, May 2025, $120M total, ~$335M valuation, microLED interconnects with SK Hynix and Lam Research as strategics), OpenLight ($34M Series A Aug 2025 led by Matter Venture Partners + $50M Series A-1 April 2026, $84M total), Scintil Photonics ($58M Series B, Nvidia investment Sept 2025), Teramount ($50M led by Koch Disruptive Technologies with AMD Ventures, Samsung Catalyst, Hitachi Ventures, Wistron, July 2025), Salience Labs ($30M Series A led by Applied Ventures and ICM HPQC, Feb 2025), iPronics (€20M Series A led by Triatomic, Jan 2025), and Oriole Networks (+$22M led by Plural, Jan 2025, ~$35M total).

The dominant VC theses in 2025-2026: (1) optical I/O and co-packaged optics for GPU scale-up fabrics — the thesis behind Ayar, Celestial, and Lightmatter's pivot from optical compute to interconnect; (2) the "laser problem" — external, heterogeneous III-V, quantum-dot, and comb laser sources (Xscape, OpenLight, Scintil, Quintessent, Aylight), validated by Meta's OFC data that 90% of optical link failures trace to lasers and lasers consume ~60% of next-gen link power; (3) fiber-to-chip packaging and serviceability (Teramount — fastest exit in the cohort); (4) optical circuit switching for AI networks (Oriole, Salience, iPronics), which Cignal AI flags as a possible bubble since Google remains the only operator deploying OCS at scale; and (5) alternative physical layers (Avicena's microLEDs, Lightium's thin-film lithium niobate). Corporate strategics are the defining feature of nearly every round — Nvidia, AMD Ventures, Cisco Investments, Samsung Catalyst, Applied Ventures, Hitachi Ventures, Koch — and generalist crossover funds (T. Rowe, Fidelity, Neuberger, Tiger, ARK) price the late stage.

Failures were concentrated in the pre-AI-boom cohort with compute-not-interconnect or consumer theses. Rockley Photonics filed Chapter 11 in January 2023 after its SPAC raised only about half of the hoped-for $323M and its pivot from datacom to wearable health sensing burned cash ($151.6M nine-month net loss on $3.0M revenue); it exited bankruptcy mid-2023 with $35M from stakeholders as a private company. Luminous Computing (photonic AI supercomputer, ~$132M raised, Bill Gates-backed) quietly died around 2023-2024 after abandoning its optical compute thesis. The broader pattern per Cignal AI: optical computing for AI training has been largely abandoned in favor of interconnect, and startups die on two identical barriers — hyperscaler design cycles move too fast to qualify unproven technology, and manufacturing partners require proven volume before integration.

For a new entrant in 2026, the observed entry pricing is: pre-seed €4.5M (Aylight, ETH spinout, co-led by Elaia and Swisscom Ventures, July 2026), seed $6-12M (Akhetonics €6M, Lightium $7M, Quintessent $11.5M), Series A $20-80M with strategic CVC participation effectively mandatory, and Series B $50-65M+. PitchBook counts 110+ US silicon photonics companies with 59 VC-backed private ones, so differentiation matters; the market signal is that acquirers (Marvell, Credo, Ciena, Molex, GF, AMD, Nokia) pay $270M-$3.25B+ for teams with production-ready CPO-adjacent technology, and time-to-exit can be under 4 years (DustPhotonics, Teramount, Nubis, Enosemi).
